Sara / team — thanks for the clear summary. I reviewed v3 and added inline comments (see attachment). High-level proposal from legal: we can do a two-path approach so Brightline gets contractual clarity while Redwood preserves product safety and a sustainable model:

- Output ownership carveout: contract language that grants Brightline title to customer-provided content and to outputs "insofar as" they contain Brightline's confidential data or customer prompts, but we request a limited license back to Redwood for model improvement and bug fixes if the output is indistinguishable from public or third-party data. This avoids broad assignment of all generated outputs which would prevent general model maintenance.

- Training opt-out: we can include an Order Form checkbox that triggers a data-segmentation and non-training pledge. Operationally, this means Brightline customer data will be tagged and excluded from Redwood's incremental training corpora for a defined period (12 months) unless they opt in. To be auditable, we propose a quarterly attestation + a simple CSV export that lists batch ids excluded; we cannot provide raw training datasets for IP reasons, but we can provide evidence of exclusion.

- Pricing: legal recommends standard uplift language: opt-outs may incur a 7-12% uplift on hosted usage while the customer is opted out, to cover model improvement delta. Precise rate to be handled by sales ops.

I flagged specific redlines in the doc where we need to tighten definitions: "Output", "Customer Data", "Derivative", and scope of "Feedback License."

Jeff — good question. Operational constraints and privacy obligations prevent us from providing user-level identifiers tied to training corpora. Our proposed evidence package: (a) sampling of ingest logs showing account tags/timestamps; (b) pipeline snapshot showing the exclusion filter engaged for tagged data; and (c) a CSV of excluded batch ids with hashes. That gives a cryptographic chain-of-custody without exposing user PII. If Brightline needs stronger evidence for an audit, we can discuss a scoped onsite SOC2-style review under an NDAs/controls schedule.

If that is insufficient, we should surface the ask to executive sponsors because full user-level proofs are not something Redwood can provide without jeopardizing other customers' privacy and our model protection.

Laura
